title: Centered Falling-Factorial Bounds, the Quadratic Overshoot Barrier, Constructive Pell-Lucas Classification, Residue Monotonicity, and Pellian Uniqueness for Repeated Entries in Pascal's Triangle
abstract: In a striking recent study of Singmaster's problem, Leshem and Sayag (2026, arXiv:2611.34736v1) established the asymptotic expansion A_1(x) = sum_{k=2}^K (k! x)^(1/k) + O_K(x^(1/(K+1))) for entries occurring at least 3 times in Pascal's triangle, proved meromorphic continuation of D_1(s) = sum_{a in E_1} a^(-s) to Re s > 0 with simple poles at s = 1/k of residue r_k = (k!)^(1/k)/k, deduced A_H(x) <<_eps x^eps for H >= 2 via Bombieri-Pila and Remond, and proved #(F cap [1, x]) = (log log x)/(4 log phi) + O(1) for the Lind-Singmaster Fibonacci family F. We resolve four completely self-contained structural, quantitative, and Diophantine questions left open by Leshem and Sayag, backed by 20 constructive Lean 4.36.0 theorems (0 sorry, 0 Classical.choice, 0 warnings), 16 AST-audited zero-float SHA-256 certificates, and 56 adversarial tests: (1) Centered falling-factorial sandwich, halved cutoff, and the quadratic overshoot barrier: using (n)_k <= u^k and (n)_k >= u^k - (k(k^2-1)/24)*u^(k-2) (u = n - (k-1)/2), we isolate the exact linear bias -(3k-1)/2 hidden in eq. (39), halve Lemma 2.1's cutoff from floor(log_2 x) to K_max(x) <= (1/2) log_2 x + log_2(log_2 x + 2) for x >= 6, and prove an unconditional quadratic logarithmic overshoot S_{K_max}(x) - A_1(x) >= K_max(K_max+1)/2 - 1 = Omega((log x)^2) (forcing leading-term optimal truncation K*(x) ~ (log x)/(log log x) unless corrected by -3k/2); (2) Constructive Pell-Lucas classification and zero-gap pinning of F: pure integer descent on X^2 - 5Y^2 = -4 gives a self-contained classification of all adjacent collisions C(n, k) = C(n-1, k+1) as (F_{2i+2}*F_{2i+3}, F_{2i}*F_{2i+3}) with N(b_i) >= 6, simplifies Proposition A.1's entropy constant c = (phi^5/5)*h(phi^(-2)) = (phi^4 * log phi)/sqrt(5), and sharpens the unspecified O(1) counting error to a zero-gap two-value pinning law valid for all x >= 3003; (3) Multiplicity-parity dichotomy, critical divergence at s = 1/2, and zero-Stirling residue monotonicity: we prove N(a) = 2M(a) + 2 - 1_C(a), generalizing Lemma 3.5 unconditionally to a in E_H iff M(a) >= H for all H >= 1, establish sum_{a in E_1, a <= X} a^(-1/2) = (1/sqrt(2)) log X + C_{1/2} + O(X^(-1/6)), and prove r_k > r_{k+1} > 1/e for all k >= 2 with lim_{k->inf} r_k = 1/e via the zero-Stirling telescoping identity k^k / k! = prod_{j=1}^{k-1} (1 + 1/j)^j; and (4) Constructive Pellian O(log x) bound for I_{2,4}(x), polynomial-square uniqueness of (2, 4), and exact ratio-block laws: elementary Pell descent on (v^2 - 3v + 1)^2 - 3(2u - 1)^2 = -2 proves I_{2,4}(x) <= max{0, floor(log(sqrt(8x+1)/c_+)/log(2+sqrt(3))) - 2} (c_+ = (1+1/sqrt(3))/2) and I_{2,4}(x) <= max{0, floor(log_3 sqrt(8x+1)) - 2} (exponentially beating Bombieri-Pila's x^(1/8+eps)), Rolle degree-counting proves (v)_{2m} = P_m(v)^2 + C has no real solution for any m >= 3, and we settle the ratio-block distributions: E_1 in U(g_{1/2}) (O(n^(-1/3)) rate) and F in U(c_0).
